# 1.

```{r}
# cov(Y1) and corr(Y1)

Z1 <- matrix(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 4, 1, 10), nrow = 4, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

G <- matrix(c(1, 0.1, 0.1, 1), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)

sigma <- 1
sigma_sq <- sigma^2

# covariance matrix: V = Z * G * Z' + sigma^2 * I
V1 <- Z1 %*% G %*% t(Z1) + sigma_sq * diag(4)

cat("QUESTION 1:\n")
cat("Covariance matrix cov(Y1):\n")
print(round(V1, 4))

# Calculate correlation matrix
D <- diag(sqrt(diag(V1)))
corr_Y1 <- solve(D) %*% V1 %*% solve(D)

cat("\nCorrelation matrix corr(Y1):\n")
print(round(corr_Y1, 4))
```

# 2.

```{r}
# same as before, Z2 is different

Z2 <- matrix(c(1, 1.8, 1, 2, 1, 4, 1, 4.2), nrow = 4, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

# G and sigma same as Q1

# Calculate covariance matrix
V2 <- Z2 %*% G %*% t(Z2) + sigma_sq * diag(4)

cat("QUESTION 2:\n")
cat("Covariance matrix cov(Y2):\n")
print(round(V2, 4))

# Calculate correlation matrix
D2 <- diag(sqrt(diag(V2)))
corr_Y2 <- solve(D2) %*% V2 %*% solve(D2)

cat("\nCorrelation matrix corr(Y2):\n")
print(round(corr_Y2, 4))
```

# 3. 

```{r}
# compare and contrast correlations

corr_Y1[1, 4]
corr_Y1[2, 3]

corr_Y2[1,4]
corr_Y2[2,3]
```
Subject 1's visit 1 and 4 correlation is 0.6633, while their visit 2 and 3 
correlation is 0.8752

Subject 2's visit 1 and 4 correlation is 08553, while their visit 2 and 3 
correlation is 0.8752

Subject 1's time points are far more clustered than subject 2's, so subject 2's 
correlation will be higher because of less time between visits.
